subject: Opsync follow-up: competitive TCO sketch + next tests
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dana Lee <dana@opsync.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Opsync follow-up: competitive TCO sketch + next tests

Dana — thanks again for the time this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

1) Recap of what Opsync is evaluating
- Real-time code-assist feature for 1500 monthly active devs, peak concurrency ~120 qps, average request size ~180 tokens in + 60 tokens out.
- Must meet median p50 latency <= 200ms for interactive snippets.
- Security: VPC/private deployment preferred; SOC2 evidence required.

2) Redwood differentiators we highlighted
- Runtime-level batching + prefix KV caching (helps for repeated context across sessions)
- Smart routing to cheaper model variants for low-risk calls, automatic fallback to high-SLA pool
- Cost transparency and token-level breakdown for chargeback to product teams

3) Immediate asks from Opsync (per call)
- A: high-level per-1M token cost comparison vs Hyperscaler baseline
- B: confirmation of on-prem/VPC deployment timing and audit logs retention options
- C: a small validation test plan (1 week) that mirrors peak behavior for batching/cache hit measurement

Attached: a quick spreadsheet sketch (Redwood_vs_Hyperscaler_TCO_v1.xlsx) — columns: baseline assumptions, per-1M token unit cost, latency SLO risk, estimated monthly spend for your profile.

Proposed next steps:
- I’ll send an initial competitive TCO sketch by EOD.
- Opsync to share any existing telemetry (token distribution, concurrency windows) — if you can drop that into the Drive doc I linked we’ll update the sheet.
- If the numbers look good, schedule the 1-week validation window (we’ll coordinate infra + a dedicated Redwood pool).

Thanks — Karthik

--
Karthik Iyer
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com | +1-415-555-0182

From: Dana Lee <dana@opsync.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: opsync-sales@opsync.com
Date: 2027-04-22T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Opsync follow-up: competitive TCO sketch + next tests

Karthik — great summary, appreciate it. A couple quick clarifications/questions before you finalize the sheet: 

1) Hyperscaler baseline — are you using their latest inference pricing (we asked them for a reserved GPU SKU quote)? We want apples-to-apples including network egress and storage if relevant.
2) For the caching: what hit rates do you typically assume for developer snippet workloads? Our internal logs show a lot of variety — some flows are near-100% context reuse, others are brand-new prompts.
3) Compliance: SOC2 attestation is required; can Redwood provide us an expected timeline for private deployment and audit logs retention policy (90 days min)?

I’ll push telemetry to the Drive link tonight (token size distribution + hourly qps for the last 30 days).

—Dana
Dana Lee
Head of Platform, Opsync
dana@opsync.com | 617-555-0221

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Dana Lee <dana@opsync.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Opsync follow-up: competitive TCO sketch + next tests

Dana — thanks, good questions. Quick answers and what we put into the attached workbook: 

1) Hyperscaler baseline assumptions
- We modeled both on-demand and 1yr reserved GPU pricing (NVIDIA L4 class proxy) and added conservative egress + network costs for multi-AZ routing. Spreadsheet tabs: "Hyperscaler_on-demand" and "Hyperscaler_reserved". We flagged where hyperscaler quotes vary widely based on committed usage.

2) Cache hit rates — assumptions we used
- Conservative scenario: 15% prefix cache hit (brand-new/low reuse flows)
- Mid scenario: 40% hit (typical developer session with repeated completions)
- Optimistic: 65% hit (highly templated flows / assistant with session affinity)

We included sensitivity rows so Opsync can drop actual hit rates and see impact on per-1M tokens. The savings come from avoided generation on the server and fewer GPU cycles due to prefix reuse.

3) Compliance / Private deployment timeline
- Redwood Private (VPC) delivery typically 4–8 weeks depending on network approvals and KMS integration. SOC2 evidence: we’ve got a current report; will share the redacted attestation. Audit logs retention is configurable — 90/180/365 day buckets, logs exportable to the customer's S3.

Next tests we suggest (short list for a 1-week validation):
- Test A (Latency smoke): 1k synthetic interactive requests at target token sizes, measure p50/p95 across model variants.
- Test B (Batching sensitivity): run the same load with and without continuous batching; measure per-token cost delta.
- Test C (Cache hit simulation): replay 24 hours of your production qps to validate real hit rate and cost delta.

We attached the workbook (Redwood_vs_Hyperscaler_TCO_v1.xlsx). If you drop the telemetry in the Drive link, Ben and I will re-run the sensitivity and post a revised per-1M token delta.

I’ll loop in Rishi on the specific test orchestration and Marissa on the CS/ops questions for audit/logs.

Thanks — Karthik

[Attachment: Redwood_vs_Hyperscaler_TCO_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Dana Lee <dana@opsync.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-22T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Opsync follow-up: competitive TCO sketch + next tests

Dana — adding a practical pricing note and a proposed lab plan.

Pricing (ballpark per-1M tokens) — post-sensitivity and using Opsync assumptions we saw in the sheet: 
- Hyperscaler_on-demand proxy: ~$1,800–2,300 per 1M tokens (depends on reserved sizing & egress)
- Hyperscaler_reserved: ~$1,400–1,900 per 1M tokens
- Redwood (combined optimizations: batching + 40% cache hit + routing to smaller model for 30% of calls): ~$650–900 per 1M tokens

Notes:
- The largest deltas come from (A) prefix cache effectiveness and (B) routing + quantized model variants for low-risk calls.
- We conservatively do not include potential engineering cost to integrate caching into your app; if you want, we can scope that separately.

Proposed 1-week lab plan (detailed steps for Test A/B/C):
- Day 0: configuration call (Redwood infra team + Opsync infra), exchange keys, confirm VPC peering.
- Day 1–3: Smoke + batching runs (collect p50/p95, CPU/GPU utilization, token counts).
- Day 4–5: Replay telemetry for cache hit measurement; tweak session affinity to see range.
- Day 6: Draft final TCO with measured hit rate and cost per-1M tokens.

If that plan looks good, we can schedule the config call for next Monday and queue a dedicated Redwood pool.

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Opsync-MAP-and-requirements.pdf (pdf)]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Opsync follow-up: competitive TCO sketch + next tests

Dana — quick operational clarifications from CS side before we lock dates: 

- Access & Roles: For the lab we request one Opsync infra engineer (SRE) with admin console access for firewall/NAT confirmations. We will provide scoped keys for test pools and rotate them after the window.
- Metrics & Logs: We will stream token-level logs to your S3; if you need longer retention we can enable the 365-day bucket (additional fee applies).
- SLA / Escalation: For Dedicated pools we can offer a 99.9% uptime SLA and a named escalation path — details to be attached in the enterprise addendum.

If Opsync can confirm the SRE contact and preferred start date (week of Apr 26 or May 3), we’ll book the infra slot.

Thanks — Marissa
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
